# MediaFlowSwift

> MediaFlowSwift is a footage manager for video creators on the Mac, made by Long Road Software LLC (Tennessee, USA). It tracks every clip from a shoot: import from cards and phones, sort and review, organize into folders ready for editing, free up space only after each copy is verified, archive, and publish to YouTube.

## What it does
- Imports from SD cards, USB drives, folders, iPhone and cameras connected over USB
- Review with frame-accurate preview, Rapid Review, star ratings, tags, notes and selects; your own categories, with optional suggestions from an on-device model or a provider you choose
- Speech transcripts, place names, weather and a shoot map
- Copies clips into category folders at each project's destination (network share, external drive or a folder on the Mac)
- Archives to numbered drives with a record of what is where; restore and relink; "Library Moved" repoints every project at a new drive
- Editing drive: move a project to a fast SSD and back, with changes carried across and checked
- Proxies for footage on a network share
- PDF, HTML and CSV reports
- Studio Pro: drafts YouTube titles, descriptions, chapters and tags; uploads to YouTube as a private draft (advanced; needs the user's own Google Cloud project); reads back views, watch time and subscribers; shared database server across several Macs

## Requirements
macOS 13 or later on a Mac with Apple silicon.

## Pricing
14-day free trial of the full app, no card required. Studio: USD 4.99/month or USD 49.99/year. Studio Pro: USD 9.99/month or USD 99.99/year. Yearly is about 17% off the monthly price. On either plan, one licence key covers up to three Macs at once, whoever uses them; a fourth Mac needs another key. Payment through Paddle, merchant of record. Full refund within 14 days.

## Privacy
No account and no usage data. The app checks for updates and, once a key is entered, checks the licence; every other outside service is off until the user turns it on.

## Guides
Plain answers to the questions people ask when moving footage off a card on a Mac. Each one says what MediaFlowSwift does and where it stops.
- All guides: https://mediaflowswift.com/guides/
- Is it safe to erase a card after importing on a Mac: https://mediaflowswift.com/guides/verify-footage-copied-before-erasing-card/ — what each check proves; on an ordinary card Clear Card only looks in DCIM, and formats import never copies (camera raw other than DNG, MTS/M2TS, MXF, BRAW, R3D, INSV, TIFF) never get a verified copy, so copy those yourself before formatting
- How to keep two checked copies of a memory card on a Mac: https://mediaflowswift.com/guides/two-checked-copies-of-a-card-on-a-mac/ — the app copies a card to one destination, not two at once; two checked copies is a sequential two-step job (import and organize, then archive to a second drive), with the destination inside the project folder
- Footage missing after moving to an external drive: https://mediaflowswift.com/guides/footage-missing-after-moving-to-external-drive/ — the Where column, Library Moved, relinking and re-checking
- How to automate video file organization on a Mac: https://mediaflowswift.com/guides/automate-video-file-organization-on-mac/ — category and camera folders, workflow templates
- How to label and catalog archive drives for video: https://mediaflowswift.com/guides/label-and-catalog-archive-drives-for-video/ — numbered archive volumes and the record of what is on each

## Blog

Articles on video storage, backup, archiving and choosing software. AI-written for Long Road Software LLC and checked against their sources; prices of other products are dated.

- All articles: https://mediaflowswift.com/blog/ (RSS: https://mediaflowswift.com/blog/feed.xml)
- NAS video storage, how to choose and structure one: https://mediaflowswift.com/blog/2026/10/nas-video-storage-how-to-choose/ — network speed vs codec data rates, capacity math, RAID levels, folder layout, verified offloads, backing up the NAS
- External hard drive organization for video creators: https://mediaflowswift.com/blog/2026/10/external-hard-drive-organization-for-video/ — folder tree, naming, Mac file systems, relinking in editing apps, backups
- Video archive storage, LTO vs NAS vs cloud: https://mediaflowswift.com/blog/2026/10/video-archive-storage-lto-vs-nas-vs-cloud/ — five-year cost per TB and restore times at October 2026 prices; MediaFlowSwift does not write LTO tape or upload to cloud storage
- Evaluating video file management software: https://mediaflowswift.com/blog/2026/10/evaluating-video-file-management-software/ — a pass/fail checklist and how the main Mac tools compare
- Checksum verification, proving a card copy before erasing: https://mediaflowswift.com/blog/2026/10/checksum-verification-before-erasing-card/ — SHA-256 vs MD5 vs xxHash, checking a copy by hand with shasum, what rsync -c and FTP/SFTP do and don't check, what a failed check means; MediaFlowSwift does not write ASC MHL files or copy to two drives at once
- Digital asset management for video production on a Mac: https://mediaflowswift.com/blog/2026/10/digital-asset-management-for-video-production/ — DAM vs MAM vs footage managers vs offload tools, what a video catalog tracks (camera metadata, XMP and sidecars, transcripts, GPS, proxies, archive drives), the shoot-to-archive lifecycle; MediaFlowSwift skips MXF, BRAW and R3D and has no XMP or client review
- How to organize video footage, picking a folder model first: https://mediaflowswift.com/blog/2026/10/how-to-organize-video-footage/ — project vs date vs shot-type folders, a date-plus-project hybrid, a naming template, migrating old footage drive by drive; MediaFlowSwift's Organize layout is fixed (Destination / Category / Camera / Filename)
- Can't find video files on an SD card, where footage hides: https://mediaflowswift.com/blog/2026/10/cant-find-video-files-on-sd-card/ — where Sony (PRIVATE/M4ROOT/CLIP), AVCHD, XDCAM, Canon, Nikon, GoPro and DJI cameras save video, searching a card on Mac and Windows, recovering a damaged card without writing to it, proving the copy before formatting; MediaFlowSwift imports MP4, MOV, M4V and AVI only (not MTS or MXF)
- Video ingest workflow, when to erase the card: https://mediaflowswift.com/blog/2026/10/video-ingest-workflow/ — the card-to-archive order (offload, verify, second copy, log, numbered archive drives, the safe-to-erase gate, formatting in the camera), how Mac offload tools verify, and what a footage hand-off file to an editor should include; MediaFlowSwift makes its second copy later with Archive to USB and writes no checksum list or MHL file

## Comparisons
Honest, dated comparisons against other ways of getting footage off a card.
- MediaFlowSwift vs OffShoot: https://mediaflowswift.com/vs/offshoot/ — both verify copies with checksums; OffShoot's strength is large-scale, multi-destination DIT transfers, MediaFlowSwift's is the review-to-archive pipeline after the copy
- MediaFlowSwift vs habitat flow: https://mediaflowswift.com/vs/habitat-flow/ — both check a card copy before you format; habitat flow has a free tier and a cheaper entry price, MediaFlowSwift covers review, archive, reports and YouTube publishing too
- MediaFlowSwift vs Finder and a spreadsheet: https://mediaflowswift.com/vs/finder-and-spreadsheet/ — what a manual workflow gives up, and when it is good enough
